slides.title: Hallboys context — what we are designing for
left_points: Acumatica is the system of record (AP, project, schedule)
3-person IT team — capacity for configuration, not custom build
One AP clerk processing every invoice end-to-end
Active Claude usage already exists across estimating, ops, finance
right_points: No replacement of Acumatica or any current system
No headcount reduction — capacity expansion only
No black-box automation on AP, contracts, or schedule
No data leaves the Hallboys Claude workspace

slides.title: How work happens today (the leaking parts)
slides.body: Three workflows where the leak above is concentrated, in your current process.

slides.title: Today's workflow — three pain points
left_points: Estimator opens 3-5 sub PDFs, hand-builds Excel comparison: 4 hrs/package
Q4 2025 example: estimator ran 11 packages, ~44 hrs absorbed
Scheduler reconciles equipment + sub list manually each Monday
Q1 2026: one concrete pour shifted, crew of 8 idle 1 day
right_points: AP clerk opens each invoice cold, posts in Acumatica AP screen

slides.title: Four workflows — each tied to one role and one number
slides.body: We removed skill governance from this version. It is a knowledge-management problem your IT team can solve internally.

slides.title: Workflow 1 — Subcontractor quote comparison
slides.subtitle: Owner: lead estimator. Anchor: Q4 2025 Westside MOB bid package.
points: Current workflow: estimator builds Excel comparison from 3-5 sub PDFs, 4 hrs per package
Intervention: estimator drops PDFs into a Claude skill returning scope deltas, missing line items, risk flags
Tomorrow morning change: estimator opens a pre-built comparison and picks the winner — no Excel build
Measurable impact: 3 hrs saved per multi-vendor package = $78K/yr at current package volume
Confidence: medium — estimate, validated week 1 by re-running 3 packages from the Q4 2025 bid log
Risks / limitations: scope nuance on unusual trades; Not available — exact Hallboys bid-package volume per estimator (week-1 capture)

slides.title: Workflow 2 — Equipment + crew schedule conflict scan
slides.subtitle: Owner: scheduler. Anchor: Q1 2026 concrete pour shift incident.
points: Current workflow: scheduler reconciles weekly schedule by hand against equipment, sub commitments, master plan
Intervention: weekly schedule + equipment list go into Claude skill that flags overlaps, missing deliveries, dependency breaks
Tomorrow morning change: Monday meeting opens with a flagged conflict list — scheduler decides each call
Measurable impact: avoiding 1 idle crew day on a mid-size job = $5,400 (Q1 2026 incident: crew of 8 × 8 hrs × ~$84/hr blended)
Confidence: medium — single Hallboys incident anchor, validated against last 90 days of Acumatica schedule changes
Risks / limitations: schedule data quality drives output quality; false positives expected first 30 days as skill tunes

slides.title: Workflow 3 — AP exception triage (0 writes to Acumatica)
slides.subtitle: Owner: AP clerk. Headline: Claude never posts. The clerk owns every approval.
points: Current workflow: clerk opens each invoice email, manually keys into Acumatica AP screen, checks PO, posts
Intervention: Claude pre-reads invoice, extracts vendor/amount/PO match, flags duplicates and pricing drift; clerk reviews and posts in Acumatica unchanged
Tomorrow morning change: clerk works from a triaged queue with anomalies surfaced first — same Acumatica screen, same posting flow
Measurable impact: 1.6x current invoice volume per clerk-day at same catch rate; defers ~$45K in OT or new-hire cost
Confidence: medium — validated through 30-day shadow mode before any clerk workflow change
Risks / limitations: false-positive duplicate flags possible; Not available — current Hallboys duplicate-invoice rate (week-1 pull from Acumatica)

slides.title: Workflow 4 — Closeout document checks against your SOP
slides.subtitle: Owner: PM on closing job. Anchor: recent retainage held 18 days past expected.
points: Current workflow: PM assembles closeout package from shared drives, owner finds gaps, retainage delay follows
Intervention: PM uploads closeout folder to Claude skill checking against the Hallboys closeout SOP — missing items, mismatched dates, lien-pay-app gaps
Tomorrow morning change: PM gets a missing-item list before sending the package, fixes gaps in-house
Measurable impact: removing one 18-day retainage delay/quarter = ~$62K/yr in working capital recovered (assumes 1 mid-size job/quarter, ~$1M retainage tied)
Confidence: medium-high — depends on Hallboys closeout SOP being current and Claude having access to it
Risks / limitations: SOP completeness; doc not in SOP will not be flagged; Not available — confirmed current SOP version

slides.title: Day-to-day workflow changes
rows: Builds 2-3 Excel comparisons by hand, ~10 hrs
Reviews 2-3 pre-built comparisons, picks winner, ~3 hrs
Estimator picks every winner; no auto-award
Opens Monday meeting with conflict list, ~30 min review
Scheduler approves every change; no auto-reschedule
~40 invoices/day from triaged queue, anomalies surfaced
Clerk posts every invoice in Acumatica; Claude never writes
Pre-checks against SOP, sends clean package

slides.title: Failure modes — what breaks, where the human stays in
left_points: Quote comparison: misses scope nuance on unusual trades
Schedule scan: false-positive conflict from stale Acumatica data
AP triage: flags legitimate invoice as duplicate (similar vendor/amount)
Closeout: misses a doc not covered by the SOP
Skill output drifts as vendors or scope conventions change
slides.right_header: Where the human still owns the call
right_points: Estimator picks the bid winner — Claude cannot
Scheduler approves every change — Claude only flags
AP clerk posts every invoice in Acumatica — Claude never writes
PM signs every closeout package — Claude only lists gaps
IT lead approves every skill version, monthly review cadence

slides.title: 60-day pilot — kill thresholds defined here, not by reference
rows: >2.5 hrs saved per package + estimator capacity for +1 package/wk
<3 real missing items found across first 5 closeouts
>5 missing items found, >1 retainage delay avoided

slides.title: Next step — schedule the day-7 baseline review
slides.body: 30 minutes with the lead estimator and one PM to pull last quarter's bid log and the closeout SOP. Pilot starts day 8 if the data is intact. We exit if it is not.
